extracted.intended_audience: Federal, State, and local agencies; Native American Tribes; industry; other organizations; and members of the public who may participate in the PEIS scoping and comment process for plutonium pit production
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for public scoping and comment on the National Nuclear Security Administration's Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement (PEIS) for plutonium pit production, including what issues and alternatives will be considered and how to participate. Intended to direct preparation, submission, and content of scoping and later PEIS comments and cooperating-agency requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline to submit these comments will be 45 days after the final public scoping meeting. As noted, the final public scoping meeting is currently scheduled for May 28, 2025, and therefore, the current deadline for comments is July 14, 2025. Comments received after this date will be considered to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission is required for full consideration; late comments may be considered only to the extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments and PII handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments on the scope of the PEIS, requests to be placed on the PEIS distribution list, and comments or questions on the scoping process should be sent to: Ms. Jade Fortiner, NEPA Document Manager, National Nuclear Security Administration, Office of Pit Production Modernization, U.S. Department of Energy, 1000 Independence Ave. SW, Washington, DC 20585 or email to PitPEIS@nnsa.doe.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before including your address, phone number, email address, or other personal identifying information in your comment, be advised your entire comment—including PII—may be made publicly available. To withhold your name and/or other PII, state this prominently at the beginning of your comment. You may also submit comments anonymously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to be designated cooperating agency
rubrics_metrics.description: NNSA requests all Federal, State, Native American Tribes, and local agencies that desire to be designated as cooperating agencies on the PEIS to contact the NEPA Document Manager at the address listed in this section by the end of the scoping period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency requests for cooperating status must be submitted by the end of the scoping period and routed to the NEPA Document Manager (contact info provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is invited to participate in scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: During scoping, NNSA invites other Federal agencies, Native American Tribes, State and local governments, industry, other organizations, and members of the public to review and submit comments on the scope and alternatives of the PEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping is intended to involve all interested agencies, public interest groups, businesses, and members of the public; input will be used to refine alternatives and scope analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: What scoping comments should address
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this Notice is to invite public participation in the PEIS process and to solicit public comment on the scope, environmental issues, and alternatives for consideration by NNSA in the draft PEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA specifically invites suggestions for the addition or deletion of items on the preliminary issues list and welcomes input on alternatives to be analyzed in the PEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting notice timing for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are future changes to [scoping meeting] information, it would be provided in a future notice posted on the website no fewer than 15 days from the planned meeting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any substantive changes to meeting logistics will be announced at least 15 days before the planned meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on land use and applicable plans and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on land use and applicable plans and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a tentative item intended to facilitate public comment; it is not all-inclusive nor a predetermination of impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on visual aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on visual aesthetics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a tentative topic for analysis in the PEIS; commenters may suggest additions, deletions, or refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on geology and soil
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on geology and soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes potential effects from construction and operations; public input invited on specific concerns or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on water resources, including floodplains and wetlands
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on water resources, including floodplains and wetlands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should identify water-resource concerns, relevant locations, and supporting data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on air quality and noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on air quality and noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis will consider emissions and noise from construction, operations, transportation, and waste handling; public input on local air/noise issues is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts to plants and animals and their habitat (including listed species)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts to plants and animals and their habitat, including species which are federally- or State-listed as threatened or endangered, or of special concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should identify species, habitats, and known occurrences; suggested mitigation or data sources are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts to cultural resources (historic and paleontological)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts to cultural resources such as those that are historic and paleontological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders (including Tribes) encouraged to provide information on cultural-resource locations and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic impacts to affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Socioeconomic impacts to affected communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include employment, local economy, demographic changes, and community services; commenters should provide locality-specific information where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts from traffic and transportation of radiological and hazardous materials and waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts from traffic and transportation of radiological and hazardous materials and waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis will consider routes, accident risk, and community exposure concerns; commenters may provide route or safety data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts from use of utilities and resource consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts from use of utilities, including water and electricity consumption, fuel use, sewer discharges, and resource conservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can identify local utility constraints or sustainability concerns to inform analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on public and workers from routine exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on the public and workers from exposures to radiological and hazardous materials during construction and normal operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis will assess occupational and public exposure under normal operations; provide site-specific exposure or health data if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on public and workers from accidents and intentional destructive acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on the public and workers from exposures to radiological and hazardous materials from reasonably foreseeable accidents, and intentional destructive acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessment of accident scenarios and security-related incidents; commenters may submit concerns or scenario data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on waste management activities and capacities (on- and off-site)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary issue: Impacts on waste management activities and capacities at on-site and off-site locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider capacity, transportation, disposal options, and potential constraints; provide data on local/regional waste facilities if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of alternatives to be analyzed (site and capacity alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the PEIS, NNSA intends to analyze: (1) site alternatives; and (2) capacity alternatives for the near term (producing pits at the current Congressionally mandated rate) and the long term (to account for potential changes in future national security requirements for pits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA will evaluate single-site and multi-site alternatives and associated activities; public input on reasonable alternatives is invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical timeframe for PEIS
rubrics_metrics.description: For analytical purposes, this PEIS will evaluate potential impacts over a 50-year period, through approximately 2075.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term impacts will be considered across the 50-year planning horizon; commenters should provide long-term data where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Action Alternative definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The No-Action Alternative will be based on NNSA's prior decision to produce 30 pits per year at LANL with surge efforts to produce up to 80 pits per year (85 FR 54544, September 2, 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The No-Action Alternative serves as a baseline for comparison; commenters may propose alternative baselines or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific preliminary reasonableness (LANL and SRS identified)
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to site alternatives, NNSA considers LANL and SRS to be reasonable alternatives because of the available facilities and infrastructure at those sites that is being/could be used to produce pits to meet the mandated schedule and capacity requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA will evaluate other potential site alternatives if determined reasonable; public may submit data to support inclusion/exclusion of sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of greenfield alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a new facility (greenfield) is likely to be considered unreasonable because it would not meet the federally mandated pit production rate in the near term and is likely cost prohibitive; however, NNSA has not decided to exclude greenfield alternatives at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may provide cost, schedule, or capability evidence to argue for consideration or exclusion of greenfield options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable NEPA authorities and level of analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: NNSA is responsible for management and implementation of the requirements of NEPA, and the regulations and policies promulgated thereunder, including, but not limited to the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, DOE NEPA implementing procedures (10 CFR part 1021), the Amendments to NEPA from the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (H.R. 3746), DOE Order 451.1B NEPA Compliance Program, and NNSA Policy (NAP) 451.1 NEPA Compliance Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PEIS will be prepared pursuant to NEPA and applicable regulations and policies and will be prepared in the same manner as a draft or final EIS and will provide the public with an analysis of the potential environmental impacts, at a programmatic level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft PEIS comment period and public hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the scoping period, NNSA will prepare a draft PEIS. The comment period on the draft PEIS will be at least 90 days. NNSA will hold public hearings on the draft PEIS in Aiken, South Carolina; Kansas City, Missouri; Livermore, California; Santa Fe, New Mexico; Washington DC; and any other location NNSA deems relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA will announce availability of the draft PEIS in the Federal Register and through other means; details of hearings will be provided in public notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of comments and Final PEIS/Record of Decision timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received on the draft PEIS will be considered and addressed in the Final PEIS. NNSA will issue a ROD no sooner than 30 days after publication by the Environmental Protection Agency of a Notice of Availability of the final PEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final PEIS and ROD timing is constrained by EPA Notice of Availability; substantive responses to comments will be documented in the Final PEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEIS preparation schedule (draft and final timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: NNSA expects to issue the draft PEIS within approximately one year of this NOI and complete the final PEIS and ROD within approximately 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule estimates are provided to set expectations for document availability and decision milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official document format and legal notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format. Until ACFR grants it official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify contents against the official edition (PDF on govinfo.gov) for legal or formal uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and need for the agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: The PEIS process is to ensure NEPA compliance for production of plutonium pits in support of ... NNSA's Stockpile Stewardship and Management Program. Per 50 U.S.C. 2538a, NNSA is mandated to manufacture no fewer than 80 war reserve pits per year by 2030; the PEIS will evaluate programmatic impacts of producing pits to meet the mandated rate (and potentially other reasonable rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should consider how alternatives meet or fail the stated purpose and need, including statutory and policy drivers (e.g., Nuclear Posture Review, Congressional mandates).
